html:
Lake Victoria is the largest lake in Africa by area, shared by Uganda, Kenya and Tanzania, and the main source of the White Nile.

The lake lies on the high plateau between the two arms of the Rift Valley. Fishing communities and the kingdom of Buganda lived on its shores. Arab traders from the coast knew it long before Europeans did.

For Europe it was the answer to an old puzzle, where the Nile began. In 1858 the British officer John Hanning Speke reached its southern shore, named it after Queen Victoria and judged that it fed the Nile. His companion Richard Burton, who had stayed behind ill, did not accept this. Speke confirmed his claim in 1862 by following the river out of the lake at Ripon Falls, near Jinja in Uganda. Their quarrel was still unsettled when Speke died in a shooting accident in 1864, on the eve of a debate with Burton. Henry Stanley sailed round the lake in 1875 and showed that Speke had been right.
sum: Lake Victoria is the largest lake in Africa by area, shared by Uganda, Kenya and Tanzania, and the main source of the White Nile.
